warnings.description: Dev#1 binary-fallback degradation: in dispatch_dedicated, the U-ok/C-fail recovery path (kernel_handle.rs ~1186-1196) does NOT recreate the binary semaphores — it cannot obtain &mut HandoffSemaphores through Arc<KernelHandleInner>, so it logs `tracing::warn!` and returns the typed compute-submit error. recreate_binary_on_error / maybe_recreate_binary_semaphores are #[allow(dead_code)] and never wired into any dispatch path (verified: only call site is the dead wrapper at line 1490). Consequence: in BINARY mode only, after a mid-chain compute-submit failure, upload_done was signaled by submit 1 but never waited; the next dispatch re-signals an already-signaled binary semaphore (Vulkan validation error / mis-sync). This is a real bug but triply-confined: requires (a) a Vulkan-1.1-only ICD with no timeline support (so SyncMode::Binary) AND (b) DedicatedTransfer mode (distinct transfer-only family) AND (c) a mid-chain vkQueueSubmit failure (OOM/device-lost). It is NEVER reachable on the timeline-primary path, which is selected on all real ICDs (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel + Mesa Lavapipe ≥1.2). It produces a TYPED error, never silent corruption. Acceptable as a documented M3.1 fixup (store handoff behind a Mutex or refactor the C-fail path to thread &mut). The design review explicitly anticipated this as a non-blocking WARNING.
warnings.disposition: accepted as M3.1 follow-up (binary-only, unreachable on real ICDs, typed error not corruption)

warnings.description: kernel_handle.rs:889 `.expect("transfer_pool_lock must be Some in DedicatedTransfer mode")` is the ONLY new .expect() in M3.0 library code (the other unwrap/expect hits are all pre-existing-on-main M2.3a code in context.rs:237/238/416/524, or inside #[cfg(test)] modules — verified via `git show main:`). The invariant is genuinely unfalsifiable: transfer_pool_lock is Some iff transfer.is_some() iff transfer_family.is_some() iff queue_mode==DedicatedTransfer, and dispatch_dedicated is only entered when queue_mode==DedicatedTransfer. It cannot panic. Still technically an .expect() in lib code; recommend converting to a typed DispatchError::Internal in M3.1 to fully honor the project ban.
warnings.disposition: accepted — provably-unreachable invariant; cosmetic ban violation only

warnings.description: readback_from_persistent_mapping swallows vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges errors with `let _ =` (kernel_handle.rs ~1468). On NonCoherent memory a failed invalidate could yield stale readback data without surfacing an error. Mitigated because (a) the always-emitted in-stream TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ barrier is the PRIMARY visibility mechanism and is additive to the invalidate, (b) invalidate only fails on OOM/device-lost, (c) on coherent memory (NVIDIA/Lavapipe) it is a no-op. Low risk; recommend surfacing the error in M3.1.
warnings.disposition: accepted — additive to the load-bearing host-read barrier

probe_results.1_persistent_map_lifetime: PASS — Drop (kernel_handle.rs 187-211) and the grow path (373-390) both order unmap(self)→destroy_buffer→free_memory for staging, then destroy/free device-local. PersistentMapping::unmap consumes self, so double-unmap and forgotten-unmap are compile errors; grow uses buffers.remove(i) so the old mapping is moved out and unmapped exactly once before realloc. map-failure cleanup in allocate_staging_buffer_cached frees memory+buffer (no leak). `unsafe impl Send` (NOT Sync) is sound: ptr is private, deref only via copy_in/copy_out under the per-handle buffers Mutex; Mutex<T>:Sync needs only T:Send.
probe_results.2_semaphore_correctness: PASS (primary) / DEGRADED (binary-only) — Timeline base+=2 via fetch_add(2,Relaxed) is monotonic and reuse-free across dispatches/errors/skips (verified reserve_timeline_block + AT-1414b). Skipped-upload compute wait = upload_signal_val-1 = base (already passed); first-dispatch base=0 waits timeline 0 = initial value, satisfied. has_uploads/has_outputs gating leaves the degenerate (n==0) path on a direct fence with no block reserved. Binary mid-chain-C-fail recreation is the only gap (see warning 1); confirmed it is ONLY a binary-fallback degradation yielding a TYPED error, with the timeline primary path fully correct.
probe_results.3_barrier_correctness: PASS — TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ barrier (srcStage=TRANSFER,dstStage=HOST,QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED,offset=0,size=WHOLE_SIZE) ALWAYS emitted on both coherency states and both queue modes (single-queue 804-818, dedicated 1112-1126). compute↔transfer execution deps provided by the timeline/binary semaphore in dedicated mode and by in-CB pipeline barriers in single-queue. flush after copy_in (before submit) and invalidate after fence (before copy_out), coherency-gated. mapped_range has no .min(alloc) clamp; returns WHOLE_SIZE when align_up(len,atom)>=alloc, else an exact atom multiple (AT-1410/1410b/1410c verified, all atom sizes incl. 65536). Host-write→transfer-read visibility relies on the standard vkQueueSubmit host-write availability for mapped memory (coherent) plus flush (non-coherent) — correct, no missing barrier.
probe_results.4_atomic_group_submit_lock: PASS — queue_submit_lock acquired once, held across all 3 submits (1140-1225), released before the host fence wait (1231). Lock order is always buffers Mutex (outer, context.rs:649) → queue_submit_lock → pool locks (inner); pool locks on error/cleanup paths are acquired under the submit guard in the same consistent order, so the wait-for graph is acyclic. No lock-order deadlock with the per-handle buffers Mutex.
probe_results.5_concurrent_sharing: PASS — device-local is VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT over [compute,transfer] only in DedicatedTransfer (concurrent_family_indices returns None in SingleQueue → EXCLUSIVE, byte-identical to M2.3a). All barriers use QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED; no acquire/release ownership-transfer pair survives anywhere (grepped). Staging stays EXCLUSIVE, touched by exactly one family per mode. No ownership hole.
probe_results.6_error_teardown: PASS — partial-submit recovery frees each CB from its OWN pool under the matching pool lock; never waits a never-submitted fence (U-fail returns before any fence wait; C-fail/R-fail call device_wait_idle before freeing in-flight CBs). Context drop: device_wait_idle → save+destroy pipeline cache → destroy transfer pool → destroy compute pool → ManuallyDrop::take device then instance (VkDevice-before-VkInstance). Handle drop destroys buffers→handoff semaphores→descriptor pool→fence→pipeline→layout→DSL→shader, then Arc<DeviceOwner>/Arc<InstanceOwner> auto-drop in field order. No leak/use-after-free found.

summary: APPROVE. ReBAR fully reverted; merged code is r1 only. All six design CRITICALs are correctly implemented in the actual code (verified line-by-line, not just designed): the always-emitted TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ barrier (both modes/coherencies), CONCURRENT device-local eliminating ownership transfer, monotonic timeline base+=2, partial-submit recovery that frees CBs from correct pools and never waits an unsubmitted fence, single-lock 3-submit atomic group released before host wait, and Send-only PersistentMapping with a private ptr accessed only under the per-handle Mutex. Persistent-map lifetime is compile-enforced (consuming unmap) on both Drop and grow paths; no double-unmap/leak/UAF. The known Dev#1 limitation — binary semaphores not recreated on a mid-chain compute-submit failure — is confirmed to be ONLY a binary-fallback degradation that returns a TYPED error (no silent corruption), is unreachable on the timeline primary path used by every real ICD (incl. Lavapipe), and additionally requires a dedicated transfer family plus a submit failure to even reach. Acceptable as a documented M3.1 fixup. Two cosmetic warnings (one provably-unreachable .expect at line 889; one swallowed invalidate error additive to the load-bearing barrier) do not block. Build/clippy/unit tests/spirv-val all clean. Merge-safe.
